chunks: Al-Muthannā narrated from Karīb al-Ṣayrafī, who said:
We were together, and we bought a bird, clipped its feathers, and entered Makkah with it. The people of Makkah disapproved of that, so Karīb sent to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام and asked him.
He said: "Entrust it to a Muslim man from the people of Makkah, or to a Muslim woman, and when it becomes restored, then let it go free."

key_terms.أَهْلُ مَكَّةَ: the people of Makkah who objected to the act
key_terms.امْرَأَةً مُسْلِمَةً: a Muslim woman who may also be entrusted with it
key_terms.اِسْتَوْدِعُوهُ: place it in someone's trust for safekeeping
key_terms.خَلَّوْا سَبِيلَهُ: let it go and release it
key_terms.طَيْرًا: a bird that was purchased and brought into Makkah
key_terms.مُسْلِمًا: a Muslim man suitable to be entrusted with it

ai.seo_question: What should be done with a bird brought into Makkah after its feathers have been clipped?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a bird brought into Makkah after its feathers had been clipped. Imam Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام instructed that it be entrusted to a Muslim resident of Makkah until its condition recovered, after which it should be released. The report reflects the sanctity of the Haram and the restrictions connected to animals within it.
